claim: V02 and V03 scope the roofless rule differently. V02 §5.7 (2), X34 (l.4095) and T-V2-59 (b) (l.3686) apply it to every roofless building — "roof kind `none`, the model's `decayed`, `ruined` and `charred` states" — so its plan's every roof bay is open. V03 §5.6 (2) (c) (l.2697) and its hand-off row to V02 (l.3236, "a wing a decay run leaves roofless") apply it only "in a decay run". V06 §3.23 (4) puts several buildings in no run: those generated `decayed` or `ruined`, those first met so in item 113's replay, and every building before M6-E. Each reads at V11's default age (`defaultAgeYears` 40). A masonry one then lands below the `roofBay` range: ashlar 0.008 × 40 → 1/3, rubble 0.44, brick 0.48, against 0.40–0.66, and before V11's rows ship every `decayed` building sits at 1/3. For such a building, V03 leaves roof bays intact in the plan where V02's exterior shows no roof, and T-V2-59 (b) fails on the fixture V03 draws.
required_change: V03 §5.6 (2) (c): "**(c) Roofless** — while the building is `decayed` or `ruined` (in a decay run, or read at V11's default age with no run in the log, V06 §3.23 (4)) and a wing's roof kind is `none` (§2.6's `RoofSpec`: …), every roof bay over a room of that wing is damaged whatever its threshold (§2.6 step 7) …; once the building's state is `decayed`, each such bay counts as reached for (b) …". V03 §13's V02 row (l.3236): "every roof bay of a roofless wing of a `decayed` or `ruined` building damaged". V03 §3.13's damage-layer row adds the edge "a building generated `decayed` in masonry, and every `decayed` building before M6-E: every roof bay of its roofless wings damaged". T-V3-39 (b) adds that fixture.

claim: T-V3-37 (V03 l. 2885) opens "the plan's one-time waits (item 119 (f)'s plan clauses; V03 §6)" and takes no bar, while its clauses name T119-2 (each wait within the comfort level), T119-3 (progress past one second), T119-4 (the `perf.qualitySpend` rows) and T119-5 (the interaction rows); the base names "T119-2's plan clauses (T-V3-37)" only. T-V3-40 (l. 2888) "takes T122-1's, T122-2's and T122-3's plan clauses" while its (f) re-runs "V12's `item122.crises` pin (V12 §2.13; T122-7)" over the plan tiles.
required_change: T-V3-37's head reads "the plan's one-time waits (item 119 (f)'s plan clauses; V03 §6; takes T119-2 – T119-5's plan clauses)"; T-V3-40's head reads "… takes T122-1's, T122-2's, T122-3's and T122-7's plan clauses)". (The registration form of (f) is the peer's VV34-r2-12.)

claim: V03 §5.6 (1) gives `roofBay` to "the roof over each room that no storeyed room of its building lies above", with no level limit. A room below level 0 that no storeyed room covers is such a room: a crypt or cellar under a solid monument's tiers, or under a stack with no storeyed wing (V03 §4.5; item 110's stepped temple and its `top: 'flat'` crypt planned alone, V03 §7). V04 §5.6 (2) gives the same ceiling `cellarVault` or `cryptVault` (V11: 0.75–1, 0.88–1, `ruined`). So one ceiling has two elements with two thresholds. Its `roofBay` (V11 0.40–0.66, `decayed`) opens a crypt beneath solid masonry "to the sky" (§8.6) at `decayed`, against V04 §5.6 (2) ("a cellar and a crypt stand intact through `abandoned` and `decayed`") and item 123 (c). V02 §5.7 (2) then reads the bay as a roof hole.
required_change: V03 §5.6 (1), the `roofBay` row: "the roof over each room at or above level 0 that no storeyed room of its building lies above, pitched or flat, a terrace's included; a room below level 0 has no roof bay, its ceiling being V04 §5.6 (2)'s `cellarVault` or `cryptVault`". J-V3.136 reads "the roof over a room at or above level 0 …". V03 §3.13's damage-layer row adds the edge "a crypt under solid tiers or under a stack with no storeyed wing" with the outcome "its ceiling V04's vault kinds, never a roof bay". T-V3-39 (d) adds "the stepped temple's crypt (V03 §7's item-110 fixture) intact through `decayed`".

claim: V03 §3.13's look row lists "save, load, undo, redo, regenerate" but not migrate, as principle (11) requires. T-V3-40, its test, has no clause for an undo, a redo or a migration ((c): two views, a scrub, a save and load, a regenerate). The damage-layer row lists "save, load, undo, redo, regenerate, migrate", but its named test T-V3-39 has no lifecycle clause. V12's `damage.breakLevel` (T123-3) runs those steps on V12's own fixtures and is not cited.
required_change: V03 §3.13, the look row: add "migrate" to the edges and "a document from before item 122's step reads `crises` absent as `follow` (§2.9), its overlays drawn as any" to the outcome. T-V3-40 (c): "… a save and load, an undo and a redo of an unrelated edit, a regenerate and a migration". T-V3-39 gains (h): "save, load, undo, redo, regenerate and migrate at the levels 0, ½ and 1 re-read the same damaged set, drawing and exports, every element breaking at the same level (V12's `damage.breakLevel`, T123-3, on these fixtures)". The damage-layer row's test cell reads "T-V3-39 (h), T-V12-56".

claim: `storeyGone` has two rules in V03. V03 §4.6 counts "per storey every `upperFloor` area of which is damaged", as V10 §3.9a and V09 ("the upper floor is gone") read it. V03 §4.5's switcher (l. 2294–2295) and §3.13's damage-layer row describe "A storey every floor area of which is damaged" by `info.damage.storeyGone`. At level 1 every `groundFloor` area of the ground storey is damaged: a rotten patch, still walkable (§8.6; T-V3-39 (d)). So §4.5 names the walkable ground storey "The ground floor is gone".
required_change: V03 §4.5: "A storey every `upperFloor` area of which is damaged (V03 §4.6's `storeyGone` rule) keeps its option, its accessible description the `info.damage.storeyGone` line". V03 §3.13's damage-layer row: "a storey every `upperFloor` area of which is damaged".

claim: V03 §5.1 *The plan in ruin* draws each damaged element "in §8.6's damaged form for its kind". §8.6 has one floor-area row keyed by position: "on any storey above ground level, a hole … the storey below seen through it; at ground level and under it, a rotten patch … still walkable". V03 §5.6 (1) makes the floor of the first storey of a wing standing on a solid wing `groundFloor` (J-V3.136: a floor on solid support; V11's late range). That storey lies above ground level, so §8.6's position rule draws it as a hole onto a "storey below" that is solid fill. Kind and form disagree for the item-110 shrines and tiers on solid platforms.
required_change: V03 §5.1 *The plan in ruin*, after "every other as built": "a damaged `groundFloor` element takes §8.6's ground-level form (a rotten patch, still walkable) at whatever level it lies, a solid wing's first storey included, and a damaged `upperFloor` element §8.6's hole".
